methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Alef Aeronautics is a Series A transportation-tech company that has raised $30M+ to date. The broader transportation sector includes 8 private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, FleetZero, and others) and no direct public comparables. However, a narrow peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints meeting valuation-tier criteria within the transportation cohort—fewer than three comparable companies aligned on stage and scale.

Stage-progression analysis was the applicable triangulation method. Using the $30M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $60M. This method reflects market practice where Series A investors typically expect a meaningful step change before Series B, though the multiplier remains contingent on execution and market conditions.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $51M to $69M (low to high), with a median point of $60M. This range reflects uncertainty around stage-based advancement expectations and the absence of transaction comps in the narrow frontier-transportation subsector. Key uncertainties include the company's progress toward near-term milestones, market appetite for the specific transportation category, and capital-efficiency relative to peers. A more precise valuation will require either identifying additional same-stage transportation comparables or updated financial metrics (burn, runway, or pre-revenue traction).
